summary: A complete target-level follow-up for high-degree root Abel–Jacobi descent. Imports the eight accepted parent GC.4 targets and supplies their family interfaces: quadratic section coordinates, nilpotent-safe affine fibre charts, intrinsic proper weighted projective quotients, canonical chart descent lines and effective atlas gluing with full faithfulness. The proper-quotient route replaces the unqualified nonproper-fibration step. GC.4 is planned, not closed: the typed generic stack-lisse adapter, actual geometric carriers and one explicit IG.0 theorem request remain.

nodes.title: Split quadratic section coordinates
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A and index types I,J, quadraticSection sends (u,alpha) in A^I x A^J to (u,(alpha_j^2)_j). In a split family chart I indexes the evaluation kernel and J the root coordinates. This is the section coordinate in E only: the full fibre-product chart sends (u,alpha) to ((u,alpha^2),alpha), retaining alpha. This polynomial function is neither asserted linear nor invertible.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including a nonreduced ring; I and J are arbitrary index types. Finite I,J are used for affine schemes.
proofSteps: Use the existing native product and function carriers and ordinary ring powers; the definition has its displayed real body.
The YZ19 split fibre description identifies the section coordinate with this function. Scalar equivariance follows from mul_pow; change of coefficient ring follows from map_pow.

For reduced A, sq_eq_zero_iff gives quadraticSection(v)=0 iff v=0. Over dual numbers this implication fails, which is why the geometric construction uses an open subscheme rather than raw nonzero ring-valued tuples.
acceptance: At I=J=Fin 1 over Z, (2,3) maps to (2,9).
Over F_3[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), (0,epsilon) is nonzero but its section coordinate is zero.

sources.match: The split evaluation description supplies the quadratic coordinate formula; the native ring formulation and nilpotent checks are its algebraic interface, not a claim that the source develops ring-valued charts.

uses.how: Identify the polynomial section coordinate after splitting evaluation and compute its effective open.
Verify that kernel and root blocks carry weights two and one.

nodes.title: The family Abel–Jacobi fibre chart
nodes.statement: For a root Picard object b=(L,K_R,iota) on X_T, with T locally Noetherian over k, put E=pi_*L, U=pi_*L(-R), G=pi_R*(L|R), H=pi_R*K_R, and q:H->G induced by alpha->iota(alpha^2). The imported high-degree vanishing yields a universally base-change-compatible exact sequence 0->U->E->G->0 of locally free sheaves of ranks a,n,rho, and H has rank rho. Define C_hat_b=V(E) x_{V(G)} V(H), with V(F) parametrizing sections of F, and C_b as the inverse image of V(E) minus its zero section. Then C_b is the actual two-pullback T x_{P_d} S_d. Etale locally on T, split R_T, choose frames and an evaluation splitting sigma; the isomorphism (u,alpha)->(u+sigma(q(alpha)),alpha) identifies C_hat_b with A_T^n and C_b with A_T^n minus the zero section as OPEN SCHEMES. These presentations and their effective opens commute with every base change T_prime->T, without a flatness or reducedness assumption on T_prime.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.
R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.
d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.

P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.
T is locally Noetherian over k for the coherent pushforward theorem; base changes from T may be arbitrary. No rational point on X and no global Poincare line bundle on a Picard scheme are chosen.
proofSteps: Import parent evaluation-surjective, SF.3/line-bundle-degree-bounds and the existing coherent sections_surjective theorem: H1(L_t(-R))=0 since d-rho>2g-2, and H1(L_t)=0. Relative coherent base change gives E,U and the exact evaluation sequence; finite etale R_T gives G,H and their arbitrary base change. The genus and ranks come from coherent Riemann–Roch.

Use GC.1/root-abel-jacobi and SF.1/two-fibre-product to identify the fixed-object two-pullback with the displayed section equation. An automorphism inducing the identity of b is the identity; the fibre is a scheme, not the weighted quotient.

Etale split R and trivialize K_R and U; frame L|R using iota. Locally split E->G. The displayed inverse is (s,alpha)->(s-sigma(q(alpha)),alpha). These are polynomial maps, with the section coordinate given by quadraticSection.

In these coordinates the inverse image of the zero section of E is defined by (u_i,alpha_j^2). Its radical equals that of (u_i,alpha_j), so its complement is exactly the usual punctured affine open. Do not identify the two CLOSED subschemes or discard nilpotents in the complement.

If sigma_prime=sigma+t for t:G->U, the transition is (u,alpha)->(u-t(q(alpha)),alpha). This quadratic transition is equivariant for weights (2,1), and the identity/composition laws follow by adding differences of splittings. The unsplit fibre product gives their canonical gluing and all base-change comparisons.
acceptance: For g=1,rho=1,d=2, the ranks are (a,n,rho)=(1,2,1), and the split equation is s=(u,alpha^2).
At d=2g-2+rho, L=omega_X(R) has L(-R)=omega_X and nonzero H1. The requested threshold cannot silently lose rho or replace strict vanishing by equality.
T may have square-zero nilpotents: the effective open is tested on all geometric fibres, not by whether its raw section tuple is unequal to zero.

sources.locator: Definition A.2, p. 515; §A.1.5, p. 517; Lemma A.9, pp. 520–521
sources.match: Defines effectiveness by geometric fibres and the two Abel–Jacobi maps, then describes a geometric fibre by the square-evaluation equation. The node promotes that equation to families and records the scheme-theoretic open and transition maps.
Nonvanishing of H1(L(-R)) forces d<=2g-2+rho, giving the strict high-degree vanishing used by the imported coherent supplier.

nodes.title: The proper scalar quotient of a family chart
nodes.statement: For b and C_b as above, define Q_b=[C_b/G_m,T]. If rho>0 the scalar c acts by (s,alpha)->(c^2 s,c alpha); its automorphism of b is (c^2 id_L,c id_K_R). If rho=0 use the ordinary scalar c id_L and weight one on s. The map C_b->S_d is 2-equivariant for this scalar action and the trivial action on S_d, hence induces h_b:Q_b->S_d. The projection q_b:Q_b->T is proper smooth surjective with geometrically connected, geometrically simply connected tame DM fibres of dimension n-1. For rho>0 it is etale locally W(2^a,1^rho); for rho=0 it is the ordinary projective bundle parametrizing lines in E. All data are functorial in b and commute with base change. Although f h_b and b q_b agree after pullback to C_b, they are generally NOT 2-isomorphic on Q_b: the scalar descent twists the Picard object. No factorization over P_d is claimed.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.
R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.
d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.

P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.
proofSteps: The scalar automorphisms of b identify each scaled section object with its original image in S_d. Their multiplication law supplies the coherent 2-equivariance needed to descend the map through the quotient; the action is intrinsic before choosing a splitting.

Use SF.1/quotient-stack and quotient-stack-algebraic for the quotient and its G_m torsor. By the family presentation, the local weights are (2^a,1^rho) for rho>0. For rho=0 the ordinary action yields P(E) and does not insert an artificial mu_2 stabilizer.

On a split nonempty-R chart the square-coordinate map from ordinary punctured A^n to weighted punctured A^n is equivariant. Before quotients it is finite free of rank 2^a, with basis the squarefree monomials in the a source kernel coordinates. Equivariance for the SAME G_m makes the descended P_T^{n-1}->Q_b representable finite locally free of that rank. It is a branched map, not a torsor under its generic sign group.

This finite faithfully flat cover by projective space proves properness: its relation is finite over projective space, hence proper over T and over the separated product; descend the proper diagonal and universal closedness. Smoothness follows from the punctured affine smooth atlas. Stabilizers are trivial when a root coordinate is nonzero and mu_2 on the remaining locus, so the stack is DM and tame in odd characteristic. These properties descend along the etale chart cover.

Import the parent weighted-cover, weighted-ramification and weighted-simply-connected nodes, with projective-space simple connectivity supplied by IG.0. A connected representable finite etale cover of a geometric Q_b pulls back trivially to projective space. A component gives an intermediate generic sign extension. Any proper subgroup admits a nonempty quadratic monomial character, ramified on a weight-one chart, a contradiction. Normality then identifies the degree-one cover with Q_b. For rho=0 use projective-space simple connectivity directly.

Under a quotient torsor the descended line bundle L is twisted by the square of its scalar line and K_R by that scalar line (by its inverse with the opposite torsor convention). This explains why the quotient square over P_d cannot be used as a Cartesian square. Only C_b=T x_{P_d} S_d has that property.
acceptance: For (a,rho)=(1,1), the fibre is W(2,1), with a degree-two projective cover; on y!=0 its coordinate is z=x^2 and the quadratic intermediate extension ramifies at z=0.
Geometric simple connectivity concerns the quotient, not the positive-characteristic punctured affine fibre.
A nonempty weight-one block is used in the monomial-chart argument; the empty-R case is separately ordinary projective space.

sources.locator: Lemma A.9, proof and simple-connectivity claim, p. 521
sources.match: The source factors the fixed geometric-fibre map through a weighted scalar quotient and uses its projective square-coordinate cover and ramification. The family quotient, finite-flat rank and properness are explicit deductions here.

sources.locator: Expose XI, Proposition 1.1, recomposed p. 219 (original margin p. 285), arXiv v2
sources.match: Projective space over an algebraically closed field has trivial etale fundamental group, including dimension zero; this is the exact scheme theorem requested from IG.0.

nodes.title: The canonical local descent line
nodes.statement: Let F be a rank-one lisse sheaf on S_d. For every b:T->P_d as in the family construction, set F_Q=h_b^*F on Q_b and M_b=(q_b)_*F_Q at finite coefficient level. Proper degree-zero base change and the geometric simple connectivity of Q_b give a canonical evaluation isomorphism e_b:q_b^*M_b->F_Q. M_b is lisse of rank one, and its pullback to the actual C_b is canonically F|C_b. Define the adic and Qbar_ell version by compatible local coefficient lattices and reduction, invert ell, and extend coefficients; it is independent of these presentations. Base change, isomorphisms of b, and morphisms of F give coherent comparison maps for M_b, including composition and identity laws.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.
R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.
d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.

P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.

F is an arbitrary rank-one lisse input on S_d; it need not be the particular symmetric local system L_d. The generic stack-lisse interfaces listed in gap GC4-LISSE-ADAPTER are required and are not claimed present in a scheme-only supplier.
proofSteps: Use the previous construction to obtain q_b proper smooth surjective tame DM and F_Q. At finite coefficient level apply ACV01 Theorem A.0.8 in degree zero: the stalk of (q_b)_*F_Q is H0 of its geometric fibre.

By the parent weighted simple-connectivity theorem (or ordinary projective simple connectivity for R empty), F_Q on a geometric fibre is constant, and evaluation of its global sections at any point is an isomorphism. Therefore the adjunction counit q_b^*(q_b)_*F_Q->F_Q is an isomorphism on all geometric stalks.

The smooth surjection q_b has sections etale locally after choosing a smooth scheme atlas of Q_b. Pull the counit back along such sections: M_b becomes a rank-one lisse sheaf there. This proves local constancy, instead of inferring it merely from the rank of its stalks.

Proper base change gives M_{b|T_prime} canonically isomorphic to the inverse image of M_b. The comparisons are the natural base-change maps and satisfy identity and composition. Pull the counit through C_b->Q_b to compare on the actual Abel–Jacobi fibre product.

Do the construction for finite reductions of local O_E lattices. Full faithfulness of inverse image along q_b (unit checked by the same fibre H0 calculation) forces the coefficient reductions and comparisons to be compatible; pass to the local adic category, invert ell and extend scalars. Glue different local lattices using the same full faithfulness. This coefficient/stack adapter is the explicit generic supplier gap, not an extra assumption of effective Abel–Jacobi descent.
acceptance: A geometrically constant arithmetic line with geometric Frobenius eigenvalue zeta_3 descends with eigenvalue zeta_3; geometric constancy does not force arithmetic triviality or sign-valued global monodromy.
For a constant coefficient line on S_d, e_b is its canonical constant-line comparison.
The construction retains rank one at every geometric point and commutes with nonflat base changes.

sources.locator: Appendix A, Proposition A.0.7 and Theorem A.0.8, preprint pp. 34–35
sources.match: Theorem A.0.8 gives proper base change for torsion sheaves on a tame DM stack over a scheme. Only degree zero is used. The lisse evaluation and local adic construction are the corollary proved in this node, not assertions quoted from the source.
The geometric weighted quotient supplies the simply connected fibres; the present construction makes the effective family descent step explicit.

nodes.title: Effective high-degree Abel–Jacobi descent
nodes.statement: At d>=rho+max(2g-1,1), inverse image along f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d is fully faithful on rank-one lisse Qbar_ell sheaves and every rank-one lisse sheaf F on S_d is in its essential image. In particular there is a rank-one L_d^Pic with a comparison theta:f^*L_d^Pic isomorphic to the unshifted symmetric rank-one L_d from GC.3. Given two pairs (M,theta),(M_prime,theta_prime) for the same F, there is exactly one isomorphism M->M_prime whose pullback intertwines the two comparisons. This uniqueness is for the normalized pair, not for the underlying sheaf with its scalar automorphisms. Descent, comparisons, tensor operations and any supplied geometric-Frobenius structure are compatible with base change over k. The empty-R branch uses ordinary projective quotients.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g.
R is a reduced finite effective divisor, including the empty divisor; rho=deg(R) is its length over k, not its number of closed points.
d is an integer with d>=rho+max(2g-1,1); n=d-g+1 and a=n-rho, so a>=1.

P_d denotes the degree-d root Picard stack of GC.0, S_d the effective root section stack of GC.1, and f=AJ_d:S_d->P_d forgets both sections. Coefficients are finite rank-one O_E/varpi^m local systems, then lisse Qbar_ell sheaves via the local adic formalism, with ell different from p.
proofSteps: For each smooth locally finite type scheme atlas T->P_d, construct M_b and its comparison using chart-descent-line. This uses a proper DM map Q_b->T, not properness or a homotopy exact sequence for the nonproper AJ_d.

By family-fibre-presentation, the actual f_b:C_b->T is smooth surjective with geometrically connected fibres. Pulling back any connected finite etale cover of connected T leaves a connected space: the projection to that cover is an open surjection with connected geometric fibres. The finite-cover/fibre-functor comparison therefore gives a surjection on pi1, so f_b^* is fully faithful on finite locally constant sheaves. The local adic formalism gives the same full faithfulness for rank-one lisse sheaves.

The double and triple overlaps of the scheme atlas over the Artin stack P_d may be algebraic spaces. Choose etale scheme covers of these overlaps and apply the preceding scheme-chart full-faithfulness argument after each refinement. On the double overlap the two M_b pull back to the same F on its actual Abel–Jacobi fibre product, so this supplies the unique overlap isomorphism compatible with those comparisons. Uniqueness makes these isomorphisms descend from the refinements. On the triple overlap the cocycle holds because its pullback holds. Effective smooth descent for lisse sheaves glues M and theta on P_d; no scheme fundamental-group statement is applied directly to an algebraic stack or algebraic space.

Check arbitrary morphisms on the atlas and its overlaps by the same full faithfulness; this proves full faithfulness globally and normalized uniqueness. It also identifies this construction with parent high-degree-descent for the specific symmetric L_d, without assuming that parent end theorem to prove itself.
Apply the comparisons to tensor products, units and any Frobenius pullback; uniqueness makes their coherence diagrams descend. Carry out the same argument using P(E) when R is empty.
acceptance: For g=1,R empty,d=1 the local quotient is P^0, while the actual fibre is G_m; the theorem descends to the Picard stack, not an assumed chosen Picard-scheme point.
For g=0 and rho=2, the stated source threshold is d>=3; it is a sufficient bound and no assertion of sharpness or descent below it is made.
A scalar automorphism c of M changes theta unless c=1. The normalized pair has only its identity automorphism, but a bare rank-one sheaf retains its coefficient-field scalars.
The source L_d is unshifted and lisse. The perverse normalization would be L_d[d] on S_d, not the object in this rank-one descent statement.

gaps.title: Typed generic stack-lisse and degree-zero proper-base-change interface
gaps.detail: The mathematical input is now precise: finite locally constant sheaves on tame DM stacks and their representable finite-etale-cover comparison; ACV01 A.0.8 in degree zero for proper tame DM Q->T; detection of lissity by smooth covers; effective smooth descent for lisse sheaves on the Artin root Picard stack; inverse image, Hom, tensor and coefficient reductions; compatible local adic lattices with isogeny and finite coefficient extension. State these on actual stack sites, retaining the stack-versus-scheme distinction. No scheme-only EDC or IG stage is asserted to provide the extension, and no unregistered ST stage is cited. The original parent ST-LISSE leaf is narrowed: a general nonproper AJ homotopy/effective descent theorem is unnecessary for the supplied proof. The root-specific quotient and gluing argument is planned here; generic stack sheaf infrastructure belongs in the proposed EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves Part II extension.

gaps.title: Actual family, quotient and lisse carriers at the pins
gaps.detail: Only quadraticSection and its five API lemmas and five ring-valued examples are typed in the compact suggested file. The root Picard/section stack two-fibre, evaluation sequence in families, scheme open, quotient stack, proper DM map, stack lisse sheaves and functors have no compatible carriers at the pins. The README specifies all geometric constructors, seven API items per construction, tests and the end theorem.
